run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-15T12:41:07Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert for otel-demo/frontend-proxy is firing because frontend-proxy's 'ingress' spans began returning HTTP 504 at ~12:41Z, when its ~15s upstream timeout started expiring. The 504s reach back to slow checkout PlaceOrder calls (~30.4s), which trace to checkout's TCP connects to the email Service ClusterIP 100.67.49.77:8080 failing with 'dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout'; the failing trace contains no email span, so the request never reached the email application. Chaos-mesh events show Schedule/otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition spawning a NetworkChaos experiment every minute from 12:40:57Z that 'Successfully apply chaos' to both email pods (email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w, email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn) and to checkout-5dccddf8bb-9cgqs, recovering ~55s later; the first spawn (12:40:57Z) precedes the alert start (12:41:07Z) and the first checkout 'failed POST to email service' log line (12:41:28Z). Email pods and all other otel-demo pods are Running and Ready with 0 restarts and were all created at ~12:07:47–12:09:45Z, ~31 minutes before onset, so pod failure or rollout is not the cause. Impact groups: frontend-proxy is affected (own 504 error spans, the alert target); checkout is affected (own error spans on 'HTTP POST' and its own timeout log lines); email shows no error spans of its own but served fewer requests with p95 latency rising from ~55ms to ~330–380ms, the signature of a network-level partition rather than an application fault. frontend showed no error-status spans itself (its calls were slow but returned 200).

claims.text: frontend-proxy is the only service with a large burst of error-status spans: over 11:41:07–12:59:35Z its spans with status_code STATUS_CODE_ERROR total ~220.95 on span_name 'ingress' and 0 on 'router frontend egress', against ~19031.9 STATUS_CODE_UNSET 'ingress' spans; its status_code label values are only STATUS_CODE_ERROR and STATUS_CODE_UNSET and its span names only 'ingress' and 'router frontend egress'.

The frontend-proxy error spans are HTTP 504s of ~15.0s: sampled error 'ingress' spans carry status tags error=true, http.status_code="504", otel.status_code="ERROR" with durations ~15.000–15.001s, and their child 'router frontend egress' spans carry error="true", http.status_code="0" with the same ~15.0s duration.

The frontend-proxy 'ingress' error ratio was 0 through 12:40:07Z, then 0.000377 at 12:41:07Z, 0.000754 at 12:42:07Z, 0.00898 at 12:43:07Z, 0.02158 at 12:44:07Z and ~0.040–0.042 from 12:46:07Z to 12:52:07Z, so onset coincides with the alert start 12:41:07Z.

frontend-proxy's error-span rate (traces_span_metrics_calls_total with status_code=STATUS_CODE_ERROR, 5m rate) was 0.2 at 12:44:07Z, 0.35185 at 12:46:07Z, 0.2963 at 12:48:07Z, 0.34 at 12:50:07Z, 0.2914 at 12:52:07Z and 0.1031 at 12:54:07Z; checkout's error-span rate rose in the same intervals to 0.1868 at 12:50:07Z, while frontend's STATUS_CODE_ERROR series stayed 0 throughout.

All of checkout's error-status spans in the window are on span_name 'HTTP POST' (~100.94 error spans over 11:41:07–12:59:35Z); their otel.status_description is exactly 'dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout' with ~30.0s duration.
100.67.49.77:8080 is the ClusterIP and port of the otel-demo 'email' Service (selector opentelemetry.io/name=email, port 8080, targetPort 8080).

checkout's own application log shows repeated 'failed to send order confirmation to "…": failed POST to email service: Post "http://email:8080/send_order_confirmation": dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout'; the earliest such line in the 12:30:00–12:44:35Z read is 2026-11-15T12:41:28.627798237Z, and the stream continues through 2026-11-15T12:48:46Z.

Full trace 4824dfdd47ada84d818501ec6a6f3c0f (12:49:12Z) shows the visible chain load-generator 'POST' (error=true, http.status_code=504, 15.0s) -> frontend-proxy 'ingress' (error=true, http.status_code=504, 15.0s) -> frontend-proxy 'router frontend egress' (error="true", http.status_code="0", 15.0s) -> frontend 'POST /api/checkout' (http.status_code=200, 30.4s) -> checkout 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' (30.42s, rpc.grpc.status_code=0) -> checkout 'HTTP POST' (30.001s, error=true, otel.status_description 'dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout'). The same trace contains no span with service 'email'.

In that same trace checkout's other dependencies all succeeded: oteldemo.CartService/GetCart 758us, oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct 424–1067us, oteldemo.CurrencyService/Convert 1.8–172ms, oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge 57.9ms, shipping '/get-quote' 72.4ms and quote 'POST /getquote' 70.7ms, all with rpc.grpc.status_code=0 — so only the email call failed.

Chaos-mesh events in namespace chaos-mesh show Schedule/otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition spawning a new NetworkChaos object every minute: -jdmmj at 12:40:57Z, -hddgv at 12:41:57Z, -mznpj at 12:42:57Z, -zl9p2 at 12:43:57Z, -7rvkf at 12:44:57Z, -8p7rs at 12:45:57Z, -4f5lv at 12:46:57Z and -5c2dr at 12:47:57Z. Each shows 'Experiment has started' and 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w', '…/email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn' and '…/checkout-5dccddf8bb-9cgqs', then 'Time up according to the duration' and 'Successfully recover chaos' for the same three pods about 55s later.

Corresponding events in namespace otel-demo show PodNetworkChaos resources being updated for checkout-5dccddf8bb-9cgqs, email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w and email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn from 12:40:57Z through 12:47:57Z.

Both email pods (email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w on node i-071e7666000f6d243, email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn on node i-0ba95c8c42c78df23) are Running and Ready (Ready/ContainersReady True since 12:07:52Z) with restartCount 0 and empty lastState; the email Service endpoints list both pod IPs 100.96.2.7 and 100.96.3.218 on port 8080; the owning ReplicaSet email-59f69bc6cf is 2/2 ready, created 12:07:49Z, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-email.

email emitted no error-status spans in the window (only status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET, ~3632.9 spans), and the traced failing request recorded no email span at all; email nevertheless kept serving 'POST /send_order_confirmation' at ~0.2889–0.348 spans/s during 12:44–12:52Z versus ~0.44–0.67 spans/s before 12:41Z.

email's own span latency for 'POST /send_order_confirmation' (0.95-quantile estimate from traces_span_metrics_duration_milliseconds_bucket) rose from ~55ms at 12:39:00Z to ~148.75ms at 12:43:00Z, ~351.3ms at 12:45:00Z, ~382.9ms at 12:47:00Z, ~371.9ms at 12:49:00Z, ~330.8ms at 12:51:00Z and ~256.7ms at 12:53:00Z, compared with the ~55ms point in the same series at 12:39:00Z.

All 22 otel-demo pods started between 12:07:47Z and 12:09:45Z (email pods 12:07:49Z, checkout 12:07:47Z, frontend 12:07:47Z, frontend-proxy 12:07:50Z), and the checkout, frontend, frontend-proxy and both email containers each have restartCount 0 with empty lastState.

frontend shows no error-status spans of its own over the window: its STATUS_CODE_ERROR series evaluates to 0 against ~83447 STATUS_CODE_UNSET spans, and its spans in the failing trace returned http.status_code=200 (slow, 15.4s/30.4s).

Likely root cause: the recurring chaos-mesh NetworkChaos experiment otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition (spawned by Schedule/otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition from 12:40:57Z and applied to checkout-5dccddf8bb-9cgqs and both email pods) impaired traffic between checkout and the email Service, so checkout's TCP connects to 100.67.49.77:8080 timed out after ~30s, PlaceOrder stretched to ~30.4s, frontend's /api/checkout exceeded frontend-proxy's ~15s ingress timeout, and frontend-proxy emitted the 504 error spans that drive RequestErrorRate. Ordering is consistent: chaos spawn 12:40:57Z, alert start 12:41:07Z, first checkout email timeout log 12:41:28Z; the impairment affects pods on two different nodes while checkout's other ClusterIP calls succeeded, which points at a targeted path-specific fault rather than a node or cluster failure; the exact action parameters could not be read.

The alert annotation's 'current: 0.2444444444444444' is most consistent with a per-second rate of frontend-proxy error spans rather than an error ratio: the measured frontend-proxy error-span rate was 0.20–0.35 spans/s at 12:44–12:52Z, whereas the error-to-total span ratio on 'ingress' peaked near 0.04. The exact alert expression could not be verified.

The impairment affected the network path to email rather than the email application: email's served-request p95 rose from ~55ms to ~330–380ms and served volume fell roughly 40% while it logged no error-status spans of its own, and the failed connections produced no email span at all — consistent with packet-level impairment of email's pod network rather than application errors or saturation.

Rejected: email pods crashing, OOM, restarting or being not-ready as the cause. Both email pods are Running/Ready with restartCount 0 and empty lastState, the Service endpoints contain both pod IPs, the ReplicaSet is 2/2 ready, and email emitted no error-status spans.

Rejected: a cluster-wide or single-node network failure. The two email pods run on different nodes (i-071e7666000f6d243 and i-0ba95c8c42c78df23) and both were impaired, while in the same failing trace checkout's calls to cart, currency, product-catalog, payment, shipping and quote all returned rpc.grpc.status_code=0.

Rejected: DNS resolution failure for 'email'. The error text shows the name was already resolved to 'dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080', which matches otel-demo/email's ClusterIP exactly, and the failure is a connect timeout rather than a lookup error.

Rejected: the namespace-wide pod recreation at ~12:07Z caused the incident. Every otel-demo pod was created at 12:07:47–12:09:45Z, at least 31 minutes before the 12:41 onset, and the affected containers have restartCount 0, so that recreation is a separate earlier change rather than the trigger.

Email's application shows no failure of its own: no STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans, pods Ready with endpoints present, and it kept serving send_order_confirmation requests throughout, so the failing component is not the email application but the path to it.

checkout is not failing generally: inside the same 30.4s PlaceOrder span its calls to cart, product-catalog, currency, payment, shipping and quote all succeeded with rpc.grpc.status_code=0 and PlaceOrder itself returned rpc.grpc.status_code=0; only the email POST produced an error span and matching error log lines.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule expression could not be retrieved: list_prometheus_rules returned no_data for rule_name=RequestErrorRate (27077cb7-e0d8-4aa4-b4b9-c6511f5ba58d-t0:f1b568f3-d6b2-4d2b-9168-4716a88f0603), for type=alert (f7072184-1319-44e5-bb3e-95d574be7533-t1:66f75cea-5cec-47d2-ae56-268f483e88df) and with no filter (f5958188-ab44-4f6d-9c52-ec7dc893c6ba-t1:fdc6b782-07f3-4038-8574-244b99fd5bb0), so the metric and aggregation behind the reported value 0.2444444444444444 remain unverified.

The NetworkChaos/Schedule specification is not readable with the authorized resources, so the action, direction, loss/delay parameters and configured duration of otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition are unknown; only its name and per-pod apply/recover events were observed.

Email container logs returned no lines for either pod in 11:41:07–12:59:35Z (email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w: 93258051-1a47-4aaa-b85b-bf4a134bc29f-t1:fd3f6c1d-5c1a-417c-9bb3-849886f4eafb; email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn: d946f67d-5ec7-4fe1-8110-cbe2b4c3716e-t1:3572e82a-d5db-45bc-8345-68931ff6be05), so email-side application handling during the impairment could not be confirmed from logs; a chaos-controller-manager log query for email/NetworkChaos in 12:35–12:59:35Z also returned no_data (c632f1d6-73a0-4b8b-9add-f971c57270a0-t2:2fa7f809-b685-4d3c-8efd-815ef16fd3bf).

One trace query returned no_data because the 12:40–12:49Z window did not overlap the stored spans (a4b5dc86-b645-40cc-8a30-87b8ac5ae99a-t0:41892f73-522c-4ce9-8a6c-ed58b8535d33); the trace was later read with a 12:49–12:52Z window, and other traces were only sampled, so the call chain beyond the reviewed trace is not fully known.

One latency sample for email 'POST /send_order_confirmation' returned no_data at 12:56:00Z (3f0f64e9-57ac-46dc-b87a-d497bab456f5-t1:a4deb2c4-e3b4-4bc6-9bea-954865e7df30), so email's p95 after ~12:54Z is unknown; the ~55ms pre-incident baseline comes from a single point at 12:39:00Z in the same series.

The checkout error-log read was capped at the newest 60 matching lines (c632f1d6-73a0-4b8b-9add-f971c57270a0-t1:ef7bab8b-2384-4b43-ad6c-5cc24c7e86d3) and the error-span sample is a truncated slice (f7072184-1319-44e5-bb3e-95d574be7533-t0:baae4291-86fa-4b0f-b6a1-7b078625060d), so earlier or later occurrences may exist unobserved.

Chaos events returned end at 12:47:57Z (the -5c2dr experiment has no recovery event in the returned set and no later spawns appear); whether the Schedule continued, stopped or was deleted after that is unknown, and the continued elevated error rates through ~12:54Z could be residual ~30s client timeouts decaying through the 5m rate windows.

The change_history integration is not available, so who or what created Schedule/otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition, and whether any frontend-proxy timeout setting changed, could not be verified.

Trace and span counts are not request counts and the traces reviewed are a sample, so the exact number of affected user checkouts and any downstream or customer impact beyond the observed 504s is not established.
next_steps: Inspect the chaos-mesh custom resources (Schedule/otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition and the NetworkChaos objects otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition-*) in namespace chaos-mesh with kubectl to confirm the action, direction, target selectors and duration, and whether the Schedule still exists.
Retrieve the RequestErrorRate rule definition from the Prometheus/Alertmanager rule files to confirm the exact expression, threshold and lookback behind the reported 0.2444 value.
Confirm with the owner whether this chaos experiment is intentional and, if so, align the experiment windows with user-facing 504s observed during each run.

If further confirmation is needed, compare node and pod network drop/retransmit metrics for the two email pods and the checkout pod over 12:40–12:48Z, and check whether the same experiment recurs in later windows.

counter_evidence.text: Email's application shows no failure of its own: no STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans, pods Ready with endpoints present, and it kept serving send_order_confirmation requests throughout, so the failing component is not the email application but the path to it.

checkout is not failing generally: inside the same 30.4s PlaceOrder span its calls to cart, product-catalog, currency, payment, shipping and quote all succeeded with rpc.grpc.status_code=0 and PlaceOrder itself returned rpc.grpc.status_code=0; only the email POST produced an error span and matching error log lines.

rejected_hypothesis.text: Rejected: email pods crashing, OOM, restarting or being not-ready as the cause. Both email pods are Running/Ready with restartCount 0 and empty lastState, the Service endpoints contain both pod IPs, the ReplicaSet is 2/2 ready, and email emitted no error-status spans.

Rejected: a cluster-wide or single-node network failure. The two email pods run on different nodes (i-071e7666000f6d243 and i-0ba95c8c42c78df23) and both were impaired, while in the same failing trace checkout's calls to cart, currency, product-catalog, payment, shipping and quote all returned rpc.grpc.status_code=0.

Rejected: DNS resolution failure for 'email'. The error text shows the name was already resolved to 'dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080', which matches otel-demo/email's ClusterIP exactly, and the failure is a connect timeout rather than a lookup error.

Rejected: the namespace-wide pod recreation at ~12:07Z caused the incident. Every otel-demo pod was created at 12:07:47–12:09:45Z, at least 31 minutes before the 12:41 onset, and the affected containers have restartCount 0, so that recreation is a separate earlier change rather than the trigger.

view.cannot_prove: Only what the containers wrote to standard output and standard error and the node still keeps: the current instance and the one before it, nothing older and nothing from a pod that no longer exists. No matching line is not proof that something did not happen; lines cut by limit or by the read limit, and lines not read, are unknown, not absent.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
